page: OVHcloud c2-15 is a virtual cloud instance built on KVM virtualization within the provider's Compute Optimized category. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an Intel Haswell-generation processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The processor does not use hyperthreading, dedicating one thread per core. Memory capacity stands at 15.0 GB of RAM, equating to 3.75 GB per core. Bundled storage includes a 100 GB local SSD, and the instance operates with no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements position the CPU in the average to lower tiers among cloud processors, reflecting the older Haswell microarchitecture. The single-core Geekbench score reaches 1196.0, and the PassMark CPU score records 6764.0, both settling in the middle 50 percent of tested instances. However, raw compute density under heavy stress tests is modest: stress-ng single-core (872.67) falls in the bottom 10 percent, while multi-core stress-ng (3481.67) and Geekbench multi-core (3698.0) place in the lower quartile. Cryptographic throughput and uncached memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 36.82 GB/sec and write speeds of 23.61 GB/sec, also sit in the bottom 25 percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dedicated physical cores and local SSD storage makes the instance viable for predictable, low-complexity applications without hyperthreading contention. However, older instruction support is restricted to AVX, FMA, and AES without modern AVX-512 or AMX extensions. Workloads that depend on high vectorized compute or heavy language model processing suffer, as demonstrated by low 7B LLM inference rates.

The hardware configuration is well matched for software compilation, basic build nodes, internal tooling, and moderate web serving or lightweight database operations. Tasks demanding modern vector extensions, high-throughput memory streams, or large-scale multi-threaded processing should consider newer processor architectures.
description: OVHcloud c2-15 is an x86_64 cloud instance configured with 4 dedicated Intel Haswell cores running at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 15.0 GB of system memory and 100 GB of local SSD storage. Designed as a compute-oriented instance without hyperthreading, it delivers steady single-core baseline metrics, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1196.0 and an overall PassMark CPU score of 6764.0. However, the older architecture limits uncached memory bandwidth and modern vector capabilities, resulting in lower-quartile multi-core stress-ng and compression results. With bundled local storage and a near 1 to 4 core-to-memory ratio, the instance provides steady execution for continuous integration workers, software build pipelines, lightweight database operations, and general back-office microservices.
